subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following nerve is a branch of lumbar plexus?

explanation.text:
The femoral nerve is a branch of the lumbar plexus and arises from the posterior (dorsal) divisions of the ventral rami of L2-L4.

The sciatic nerve, posterior femoral cutaneous nerve, and nerve to obturator internus are part of the sacral plexus.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: A patient presents with tingling, numbness, and burning pain in the outer part of the right thigh. There is no motor dysfunction. What is the root value of this patient's affected nerve?

explanation.text:
The scenario is suggestive of meralgia paresthetica, in which the lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh is affected. Its root value is L2 and L3.

It arises from the posterior divisions of the ventral rami of L2 and L3 and supplies the skin of the anterior and lateral surfaces of the thigh up to the knee.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: The femoral nerve is split into the anterior and posterior divisions by which of the following arteries?

explanation.text:
The femoral nerve is split into anterior and posterior divisions by the lateral circumflex femoral artery.

Course of femoral nerve: it arises from posterior divisions of ventral rami of L2-L4 on the posterior abdominal wall, enters the femoral triangle under the inguinal ligament, lies lateral to the femoral artery and outside the femoral sheath, and divides into anterior and posterior branches around the lateral circumflex femoral artery.

Source note: the obturator nerve is divided into anterior and posterior divisions by obturator externus in the upper part and adductor brevis in the lower part.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: A 60-year-old woman after a trivial fall presents with pelvic fracture along with left femoral nerve injury. The function of all of the following muscles will be affected except:

explanation.text:
Gracilis is supplied by the obturator nerve and not the femoral nerve, so its function is not affected by femoral nerve injury.

Before entering the thigh, the femoral nerve supplies iliacus and pectineus. Its anterior division supplies sartorius and cutaneous branches to the anteromedial thigh. Its posterior division supplies quadriceps femoris, the knee joint, and sensation to the medial leg through the saphenous nerve.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: In a patient, following venous cut down for access to the great saphenous vein, sensation over the medial side of the leg was lost. The affected nerve is a branch of which of the following nerves?

explanation.text:
Loss of sensation over the medial side of the leg denotes injury to the saphenous nerve, a branch of the posterior division of the femoral nerve.

The saphenous nerve is the largest cutaneous branch of the femoral nerve. It enters the adductor canal, crosses anterior to the femoral artery to lie medially, leaves the canal by piercing fascia lata between gracilis and sartorius, and then descends along the medial tibial border with the long saphenous vein.

It supplies the skin on the medial side of the knee, leg and foot as far as the first metatarsophalangeal joint.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Obturator nerve block is performed on a patient with severe chronic hip pain. Anterior division of this nerve innervates all of the following muscles except:

explanation.text:
The anterior division of the obturator nerve does not innervate adductor magnus; adductor magnus is supplied by the posterior division.

The obturator nerve arises from anterior divisions of ventral rami L2-L4 and divides into anterior and posterior branches near the obturator foramen.

Anterior division supplies pectineus, adductor longus, adductor brevis and gracilis. Posterior division supplies adductor magnus and obturator externus, and may also supply adductor brevis.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following nerve does not innervate the muscles of the gluteal region?

explanation.text:
The sciatic nerve does not innervate muscles of the gluteal region.

It is formed by L4-S3 components of the sacral plexus, exits through the greater sciatic foramen inferior to piriformis, descends in the posterior thigh and divides into tibial and common peroneal nerves proximal to the knee.

The tibial component supplies semimembranosus, semitendinosus, the ischial part of adductor magnus and long head of biceps femoris. The common fibular component supplies the short head of biceps femoris.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: A 40-year-old man comes with a history of a hip fracture which was treated surgically, four months ago. You observe him walking with the gait shown below. Injury to which of the following nerves is most likely in this patient?

explanation.text:
The gait shown is characteristic of a left superior gluteal nerve injury causing a positive Trendelenburg sign.

Gluteus medius and minimus are supplied by the superior gluteal nerve. When the opposite leg is lifted, these abductors on the supported side raise the pelvis on the unsupported side and keep the trunk upright.

With paralysis, the pelvis sinks on the unsupported normal side when standing on the affected limb. In the figure, lifting the right leg causes the right side of the pelvis to tilt down, indicating a left-sided abductor mechanism lesion.

Inferior gluteal nerve supplies gluteus maximus.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Foot drop is caused by damage to:

explanation.text:
Foot drop is caused by damage to the common peroneal nerve.

The common peroneal nerve is a component of the sciatic nerve. It curves around the neck of the fibula deep to peroneus longus and divides into superficial and deep peroneal nerves.

The superficial peroneal nerve supplies peroneus longus and brevis and most of the dorsum of the foot. The deep peroneal nerve supplies the anterior compartment dorsiflexors, extensor digitorum brevis, first two dorsal interossei and the first web space.

Common peroneal injury causes weak dorsiflexion/foot drop, loss of eversion, loss of toe extension, and sensory loss over the anterolateral leg and dorsum of the foot.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: A 45-year-old man came for his cast removal after a right tibial fracture. You noted that the patient lifted his right leg high to take a step. On examination, the right foot was inverted and sensory loss was present on the whole dorsum of the right foot. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected in this patient?

explanation.text:
The affected nerve is the common fibular (common peroneal) nerve.

It is derived from L4, L5, S1 and S2 ventral rami through the sciatic nerve and runs along the lateral popliteal fossa to the fibular head, then winds around the fibular neck where it is commonly injured, including by a tight plaster cast.

It divides into superficial and deep fibular nerves. Injury produces foot drop, loss of eversion, loss of toe extension, and sensory loss over the anterolateral leg and dorsum of foot.

Source note: ankle reflex is preserved in common peroneal nerve palsy.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following does not share its nerve supply with the rest of the given muscles?

explanation.text:
Peroneus longus is supplied by the superficial peroneal nerve; the other listed muscles are supplied by the deep peroneal nerve.

The anterior compartment of the leg is supplied by the deep peroneal nerve and includes tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, extensor digitorum longus and peroneus tertius.

The lateral compartment contains peroneus longus and brevis and is supplied by the superficial peroneal nerve. The posterior compartment is supplied by the tibial nerve.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: In a patient with Morton's neuroma, branches of which of the following nerves will get entrapped?

explanation.text:
Morton's neuroma may occur due to entrapment of branches of the medial plantar nerve.

The source identifies entrapment of the third common digital nerve, a branch of the medial plantar nerve, as the common pattern.

The medial plantar nerve can also be compressed at the Knot of Henry, where the flexor hallucis longus tendon passes deep to the flexor digitorum longus tendon to reach the medial sole.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: What is the root value of cremasteric reflex?

explanation.text:
The cremasteric reflex is mediated by L1 and L2. Stroking the medial thigh produces ipsilateral elevation of the testicle.

Afferent limb: femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve. Efferent limb: genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following is not a branch of the femoral artery?

explanation.text:
The deep circumflex iliac artery is a branch of the external iliac artery, not the femoral artery.

The femoral artery is the continuation of the external iliac artery behind the inguinal ligament. It descends through the femoral triangle and adductor canal, passes through the adductor hiatus and continues as the popliteal artery.

Branches listed by the source include superficial epigastric, superficial circumflex iliac, superficial external pudendal, deep external pudendal, muscular branches, profunda femoris and descending genicular artery.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following artery does not take part in the cruciate anastomosis?

explanation.text:
The superior gluteal artery does not contribute to the cruciate anastomosis.

Cruciate anastomosis lies at the level of the lesser trochanter and is formed by transverse branches of the medial and lateral circumflex femoral arteries, the descending branch of the inferior gluteal artery, and the ascending branch of the first perforating artery.

The source notes the clinical importance of lower-limb arterial anastomoses in trauma and hemorrhage control.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: A 60-year-old man presented with pain while walking after a prolonged flight travel. Ultrasonography revealed thrombus in the short saphenous vein. If the thrombus gets dislodged, it is likely to enter which of the following veins first?

explanation.text:
A thrombus in the short saphenous vein may dislodge and enter the popliteal vein first. It can then travel to the right heart and potentially cause pulmonary embolism.

The short saphenous vein continues from the lateral side of the dorsal venous arch, passes behind the lateral malleolus and drains into the popliteal vein in the popliteal fossa. The popliteal vein continues proximally as the femoral vein.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: What are above knee perforators known as?

explanation.text:
Above-knee perforators are known as Dodd veins.

Perforator veins connect the deep and superficial venous systems. The source names proximal thigh perforators as Hunter perforators, distal thigh/above-knee perforators as Dodd perforators, below-knee perforators as Boyd perforators, and calf perforators as Cockett perforators.
